extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism ontology record. Automated framework locator placeholders were replaced with paper-specific direct assay claims from XML/PDF/OA figure evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Salivaricin 9 is bactericidal against susceptible Micrococcus luteus cultures, with loss of subsequent growth after peptide addition.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports bactericidal/lytic activity in tested susceptible indicator bacteria; it does not establish a human-cell toxicity profile.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SYTOX Green membrane-permeabilization assays show salivaricin 9 compromises the cytoplasmic membrane of Streptococcus equisimilis and Corynebacterium spp.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The assay supports membrane permeabilization in the tested Gram-positive indicators and should not be generalized to all bacteria.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Propidium iodide flow cytometry shows increased membrane permeability in Micrococcus luteus ATCC10240 after salivaricin 9 exposure at multiples of its MIC.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The source supports pore-forming membrane disruption; exact MFI values were figure-level and were not normalized into numeric database fields.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Scanning electron microscopy shows pore-like morphological damage in Micrococcus luteus, Streptococcus equisimilis, and Corynebacterium spp cells treated with salivaricin 9.
mechanism_claims.limitations: SEM supports visible cell envelope damage in the tested strains; it is qualitative and not a standalone binding-target assay.

unsupported_or_rejected_claims.reason: The local source mentions tetracycline/protein synthesis as a comparator/control context, not as a direct mechanism for salivaricin 9.
SYTOX Green and propidium iodide are membrane-integrity reporters; local evidence does not support salivaricin 9 as a nucleic-acid-binding mechanism.
